drills.family_note: круг 105: чистый слот, источник ложного подозрения переписан — вместо предложения партнёра, которое якобы открывает закрытое окно, здесь объявленный потолок расходов, который якобы связывает. Отвергается другим счётом: не календарём, а разбором шести строк по роду числа и сложением в трёх прочтениях слова spend — 250 (всё) / 220 (деньги со счёта) / 160 (невозвратное) против 300. F0 сохраняется: kill set пуст.

reference.en:
**Conclusion.** Ask which ideas put a different product through capacity that is already paid for — and, when the ceiling arrives, ask what it actually meters before adding the six requirements up and before dropping anything.

**Where the winter money is.** Twelve shops are leased for the full year and the staff are salaried, so between November and March the rent and the payroll are spent whether anyone walks in or not. That splits the six ideas cleanly. Service, storage, indoor training and winter kit all sell something different through a floor and a team that are standing there anyway. A December discount on last season's bicycles sells the same thing to the same catchment at a lower price and takes margin from the season that already works. The two classes are not comparable on headline revenue, which is why the first question is what the catchment actually does in winter and what each idea needs that the shops do not already have.

**Second move, and the whole test.** Finance sets a ceiling of €300 000 of incremental spend, and the instinct is to start cutting from the top: the €95 000 studio looks like the obvious casualty. Ask what the ceiling meters before adding, because the six lines are not one kind of number. Three are cash that does not come back: the bench and marketing at €40 000, the fit-out at €95 000, the racking at €25 000. One is €60 000 of stock, cash out that converts back into cash. One is €0, because the ski operator fits out at his own expense. One is €30 000 of margin given up, which never leaves the bank account at all. That gives three defensible totals against a ceiling of €300 000 — everything the initiatives consume, €250 000; cash out of the door, €220 000; non-recoverable spend, €160 000 — and all three clear it. The ceiling does not bind under any reading of the word it is written in. Nothing has to be dropped, and the request to drop something was itself the trap.

**The reflex punished here.** A stated limit reads as a binding limit, because in most cases it is one, and because cutting looks decisive while adding looks passive. Killing the largest idea is the fluent move and it is wrong twice over: size is not a ground for culling when the total fits, and the €95 000 studio is the one idea that puts a genuinely different product on the idle floor. A silent zero does not pass either. Refusing to cut without showing the sum is indistinguishable from not having looked — and a sum that mixes forgone margin with cash without saying so has been performed rather than read.
reference.ru:
**Вывод.** Спроси, какие идеи прогоняют другой продукт через мощность, которая уже оплачена, — а когда придёт потолок, спроси, что именно он меряет, и лишь потом складывай шесть требований и решай, что вычёркивать.

**Где зимой лежат деньги.** Двенадцать магазинов арендованы на весь год, персонал на окладе — значит с ноября по март аренда и фонд оплаты потрачены независимо от того, зашёл ли кто-нибудь. Это чисто делит шесть идей. Сервис, хранение, зал станков и зимняя экипировка продают другое через торговый зал и людей, которые и так стоят. Декабрьская скидка на прошлогодние велосипеды продаёт то же самое тому же охвату дешевле и забирает маржу у сезона, который и без того работает. Два класса несравнимы по валовой выручке, поэтому первый вопрос — что охват реально делает зимой и чего каждой идее не хватает из того, чего у магазинов нет.

**Второй ход, и в нём вся проверка.** Финансы объявляют потолок в €300 000 дополнительных расходов, и инстинкт — резать сверху: студия за €95 000 выглядит очевидной жертвой. Сначала спроси, что потолок меряет, потому что шесть строк — числа трёх разных родов. Три — деньги, которые не возвращаются: верстак с маркетингом за €40 000, отделка студии за €95 000, стеллажи за €25 000. Одна — €60 000 товарного запаса: деньги вышли, но обращаются обратно в деньги. Одна — €0, потому что лыжный оператор оборудует зал за свой счёт. Одна — €30 000 упущенной маржи, которая вообще не покидает счёт. Отсюда три защитимых итога против потолка €300 000: всё, что инициативы потребляют, — €250 000; деньги, вышедшие со счёта, — €220 000; невозвратные расходы — €160 000. Проходят все три. Потолок не связывает ни при одном прочтении слова, которым он написан. Вычёркивать не надо ничего, а сама просьба вычеркнуть и была ловушкой.

**Какой рефлекс здесь наказывается.** Объявленный предел читается как связывающий, потому что чаще всего он таков и потому что резать выглядит решительно, а складывать — пассивно. Убить самую крупную идею — беглый ход, и он неверен дважды: размер не основание для отсева, когда сумма проходит, и именно студия за €95 000 — единственная идея, ставящая на простаивающий пол по-настоящему другой продукт. Молчаливый ноль тоже не проходит: отказ резать без предъявленной суммы неотличим от того, что кандидат просто не смотрел, — а сумма, в которой упущенная маржа сложена с деньгами и об этом не сказано, посчитана, но не прочитана.

mehanizm.naive: принимает объявленный потолок за связывающее ограничение и вычёркивает самую дорогую идею, не сложив требования всех и не спросив, что потолок меряет
mehanizm.correct: разносит шесть строк по роду числа (невозвратные деньги, оборотный запас, упущенная маржа) и складывает в каждом прочтении: 250 / 220 / 160 против 300 — потолок слаб при любом
mehanizm.why: объявленное ограничение связывает только тогда, когда сумма требований, выраженная в тех же единицах, что и предел, его превышает; здесь требования трёх разных родов, и ни одно прочтение не даёт связывания

drills.title: Listed and Locked
drills.prompt: Vreskoval owns 6 city hotels. Occupancy is 81% and the board wants more revenue from the flagship property. What are the options?
facts: The flagship is a nineteenth-century building, **a listed heritage site**: changes to the layout, the façade and load-bearing structures are prohibited by the preservation covenant.
74 rooms, 88% occupancy, average rate 9% below market.
The ground floor is let to a restaurant tenant; that lease expires in six months.
The conference hall is booked 3 days a week.

key.load:
**`LOAD` — revenue off the existing stock: rate, segment, and use of non-room space.**
The culling fact is **regulatory**: any idea requiring structural work (adding rooms, splitting existing ones, adding a floor, altering the façade) is dead under the listed-building covenant. What remains is whatever leaves the structure alone.
*The second variant of the class. The culling fact: BR-001 technical (certification), BR-017 regulatory (listed status). One mechanic, two natures of prohibition.*
*Grounding: Opus Two (D24) — the site is unusable and a whole class of ideas falls away; Mustard Clinic (K20) — the patient mix does not shift over a short horizon; Salty Sole Shoe (K20).*
key.cover: **`COVER`:** A. rate and demand segmentation · B. non-room space (restaurant, conference room, roof, basement within what is permitted) · C. sales channels and direct booking
key.dead:
**`DEAD`:**

| Branch | What kills it |
|---|---|
| Add rooms by reconfiguring the layout | prohibited by the listed-building covenant |
| Add a floor or alter the façade | the same |
| "Refurbish to move up a class" without stating what is actually permitted | fails `[GROUND]` |
key.grader:
### Grader

- **load_syn:** rate · revenue per room · revpar · existing stock · without structural work · guest segment
- **cover.A (rate and segment):** raise the rate · dynamic pricing · corporate segment · extended stay
- **cover.B (non-room space):** restaurant · conference room · space to let · roof · event
- **cover.C (channels):** direct booking · sales channel · aggregator commission · loyalty programme
- **dead.D1:** more rooms · reconfigure the layout · split the rooms
- **dead.D2:** add a floor · alter the façade · build an extension
- **dead.D3:** refurbish · refresh the interiors

---

---

---

---

---

---

reference.en:
Take the additional revenue off the assets the covenant does not touch — rate, guest mix and the non-room space — because the listed status deletes the entire capacity branch before the brainstorm even starts.

The flagship runs at 88% occupancy against 81% across the group and sells 9% below market rate on 74 rooms. That combination says the room side is close to full and underpriced: a pricing and segmentation problem, not a volume one. The conference hall is booked 3 days out of 7, 43% of the week — the gap against the rooms' 88% is 45 percentage points of utilisation, and unlike the rooms the hall can be filled without moving a single wall. The restaurant lease is the other unlocked asset and the only date in the record: in six months that floor is either re-let on the old terms or repriced, and after the expiry nobody has to ask the preservation authority anything.

The reflex punished here is answering 'more revenue from a hotel' with capacity — add rooms, split the large ones, add a floor, refurbish up a class. High occupancy reads as an invitation to build, and every one of those ideas is dead on a covenant that prohibits changes to layout, façade and load-bearing structures. Worse, the covenant is stated as a property of the building rather than flagged as a constraint, so it is easy to read past it and produce a list that is formally complete and entirely unusable. 'Refurbish to move up a class' fails for the same reason unless the candidate says what is actually permitted inside a listed shell.

What remains is genuinely large: 9% below market on a house that is already 88% full is the cheapest revenue in the record, because the demand needed to support the rate is already standing at the desk.
reference.ru:
Снимай дополнительную выручку с активов, которых охранное обязательство не касается, — с тарифа, микса гостей и не-номерных площадей: статус памятника вычёркивает всю ветку мощности ещё до начала брейншторма.

Флагман загружен на 88% против 81% по группе и продаётся на 9% ниже рынка при 74 номерах. Эта комбинация говорит, что номерная сторона почти полна и недооценена по цене: это задача тарифа и сегментации, а не объёма. Конференц-зал занят 3 дня из 7, то есть 43% недели, — разрыв с 88% номеров составляет 45 п.п. загрузки, и, в отличие от номеров, зал наполняется без переноса единой стены. Второй свободный актив — аренда ресторана, и это единственная дата в записи: через шесть месяцев этаж либо продлевается на старых условиях, либо переоценивается, и после истечения срока разрешения ни у кого спрашивать не нужно.

Рефлекс, который здесь наказывается, — отвечать на «больше выручки от отеля» мощностью: добавить номера, разделить крупные, надстроить этаж, сделать ремонт под более высокий класс. Высокая загрузка читается как приглашение строить, и все эти идеи мертвы на обязательстве, запрещающем менять планировку, фасад и несущие конструкции. Хуже того, статус памятника подан как свойство здания, а не помечен как ограничение, поэтому его легко проскочить и выдать список, формально полный и полностью непригодный. «Ремонт для перехода в другой класс» падает по той же причине, если кандидат не говорит, что именно разрешено внутри охраняемой оболочки.

То, что остаётся, действительно велико: 9% ниже рынка при загрузке 88% — самая дешёвая выручка в этой записи, потому что спрос, нужный для удержания тарифа, уже стоит на стойке.

mehanizm.naive: предлагает поднять доход через изменение конструкции объекта
mehanizm.correct: предлагает поднять его на существующем фонде — тарифом, сегментом, использованием непрофильных площадей
mehanizm.why: охранный статус убивает весь класс конструктивных идей независимо от их качества

drills.title: Half a Season
drills.prompt: Yalcrindo grows ornamental plants. Its largest buyer — a DIY chain — is not renewing, removing **1.8 million units a year**, 35% of output. Planting for next season starts in six weeks. What can we do?
facts: The volume leaving is **1.8 million units a year**.
The three remaining chain customers take 2.1 million between them; their orders for next season are already confirmed and up **6% (≈126 thousand)**.
The company's own retail garden centre sells **340 thousand a year**, and the site can hold no more than **+50%** (≈170 thousand).

The regional wholesale market of landscaping contractors is **900 thousand a year**; Yalcrindo's share today is 11% (≈99 thousand), and a realistic gain over one season is put at **+15 p.p.** (≈135 thousand).
Disposal of unsold planting stock costs 4 currency units per unit.
A chain's procurement cycle for a new supplier runs a year; listings for next season are already closed.

key.load:
**`LOAD` — add the measures up and present the gap.**
126 + 170 + 135 = **431 thousand against the 1 800 thousand being lost.** Less than a quarter is covered. A strong candidate works this out **unaided** and moves the conversation from "what do we replace it with" to "how much do we cut the planting by" — at 4 per unit disposed of, the price of a planning error is computed directly.
*The second variant of the class. Difference from BR-007: there the quantified measures cover under a third and the biggest branch cannot be sized at all; here it closes by a quarter, and the conclusion turns towards cutting production volume.*
*Grounding: Build, Baby, Build! (W23); GGC Health (S19); Cents and Sensibility (W23); Kellogg in India (K20).*
key.cover: **`COVER`:** A. existing customers · B. our own retail channel · C. new sales segments (landscaping contractors, municipal planting)
key.dead: **`DEAD`:** exporting live plants (quarantine periods do not fit inside six weeks) · "find a new chain customer" ignoring the chains' procurement cycle (a year) · "step up sales" (fails `[GROUND]`).

cull.new_fact: The agronomist reminded us: the planting plan for next season is locked in six weeks and cannot be changed after that date — the plants take two seasons to grow.
team_ideas: Take more volume from the three chains we already supply.
Expand our own garden centre.
Go after landscaping contractors.
Find a new chain customer to replace the one that left.
Cut the planting plan for next season.
Plant against future demand and sell a season later.
cull.peridea_raw:
**Per-idea analysis (`[CULL-PERIDEA]`):**

| # | Idea | What the fact does to it | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Take more from existing customers | the orders are already confirmed, the ceiling is +126 thousand — the idea is alive, but its contribution is capped | alive |
| 2 | Expand the garden centre | the fact does not touch it | alive |
| 3 | Landscaping contractors | the fact does not touch it | alive |
| 4 | A new chain customer | a chain's procurement cycle is a year; it cannot be done before the planting plan is fixed | **killed** · `does not answer the question asked` |
| 5 | Cut the planting plan | the fact makes it **urgent**, not dead | alive |
| 6 | Plant against future demand | two seasons of growing plus 4 per unit disposed of: a bet on demand nobody has confirmed, with the price of being wrong already known | **killed** · `not testable` |

**Kill set: `{4, 6}`, on different grounds.**

**`[NOSELF]`:** all five numbers are given as separate pieces of background about the channels; adding them up and comparing with 1.8 million is the candidate's work. The words "not enough" do not appear in the text.

key.grader:
### Grader

- **load_syn:** not enough · gap · covers a quarter · sum of the measures · cut the planting · plant less · hole
- **cover.A (existing customers):** the chains we supply · three customers · confirmed orders
- **cover.B (retail):** garden centre · own retail · expand the site
- **cover.C (new segments):** landscaping contractor · municipal planting · municipal · wholesale
- **dead.D1:** export · ship abroad · quarantine
- **dead.D2:** new chain customer · replace the chain · find a chain
- **dead.D3:** step up sales · marketing · promotion

---

---

---

---

---

reference.en:
Add the measures up before proposing them — Yalcrindo's three quantifiable channels do not replace the buyer, and the decision on the table is how far to cut next season's planting.

The three remaining chains have already confirmed orders up 6%, about 126 thousand. The company's own garden centre sells 340 thousand and the site holds no more than +50%, about 170 thousand. A realistic one-season gain of 15 p.p. on a 900-thousand regional contractor market is about 135 thousand. Together that is 431 thousand against 1.8 million units leaving: the gap is 1 369 000 units, 76% of the volume lost, and nothing in the record closes it inside six weeks. Each measure sounds sufficient inside its own sentence — '+50% of our own retail' is a big relative number and 170 thousand units, 9% of the hole, in absolute.

That is the reflex punished here: finishing at the list. Six weeks of pressure invites naming channels and stopping there, and every relative figure in the record flatters — +6%, +50%, +15 p.p. — while the absolute they sum to is under a quarter of the loss. Nowhere does the record use the word 'not enough'; the arithmetic is left for the candidate, and a candidate who never performs it recommends replacing a buyer that cannot be replaced. Once it is performed the conversation moves to the volume that should not be planted at all, and the price of getting that wrong is already in the record at 4 a unit to dispose of.

Second move. The agronomist's fact — the planting plan locks in six weeks and the crop takes two seasons — kills ideas 4 and 6, on different grounds. A new chain customer is not contradicted by anything: a chain's procurement cycle runs a year and next season's listings are closed, so the idea simply answers a different question than the one asked. Planting against future demand is feasible and dies for another reason: nothing in the record confirms that demand, while the cost of being wrong is already priced at 4 a unit. Idea 5, cutting the planting plan, is the one candidates want to cut because it reads as surrender — the fact makes it urgent, not dead. Ideas 1, 2 and 3 survive with their contributions capped at the numbers above.
reference.ru:
Сложи меры, прежде чем их предлагать: три измеримых канала Yalcrindo не заменяют покупателя, а решение на столе — насколько глубоко сократить посадку следующего сезона.

Три оставшиеся сети уже подтвердили рост заказов на 6% — около 126 тысяч. Собственный садовый центр компании продаёт 340 тысяч, и площадка выдержит не больше +50% — около 170 тысяч. Реалистичный прирост за один сезон в 15 п.п. на региональном рынке подрядчиков объёмом 900 тысяч — это около 135 тысяч. Вместе это 431 тысяча против 1.8 миллиона уходящих единиц: разрыв — 1 369 000 единиц, 76% потерянного объёма, и ничто в записи не закрывает его за шесть недель. Каждая мера выглядит достаточной внутри собственной фразы: «+50% нашей собственной розницы» — крупное относительное число, а в абсолютном выражении это 170 тысяч единиц, 9% дыры.

Это и есть рефлекс, который здесь наказывается: закончить на списке. Шесть недель давления подталкивают назвать каналы и на этом остановиться, и каждая относительная цифра в записи льстит — +6%, +50%, +15 п.п., — тогда как в абсолютном выражении их сумма не дотягивает и до четверти потери. Нигде запись не употребляет слова «не хватает»: арифметика оставлена кандидату, и кандидат, который её так и не выполнит, порекомендует заменить покупателя, которого заменить нельзя. Как только она выполнена, разговор переходит к объёму, который не следует сажать вовсе, а цена ошибки здесь уже есть в записи — 4 на единицу за утилизацию.

Второй ход. Факт агронома — план посадки фиксируется через шесть недель, а культура растёт два сезона — убивает идеи 4 и 6, причём на разных основаниях. Новому сетевому клиенту не противоречит ничто: закупочный цикл сети идёт год, а листинги следующего сезона уже закрыты, поэтому идея просто отвечает не на тот вопрос, который задан. Сажать под будущий спрос выполнимо, и умирает эта идея по другой причине: спрос ничем в записи не подтверждён, тогда как цена ошибки уже оценена в 4 на единицу. Идею 5, сокращение плана посадки, кандидаты как раз и хотят вычеркнуть, потому что она читается как капитуляция, — факт делает её срочной, а не мёртвой. Идеи 1, 2 и 3 переживают проверку, и их вклад ограничен числами выше.

mehanizm.naive: перечисляет каналы замещения ушедшего объёма, не складывая их и не сравнивая с потерей
mehanizm.correct: складывает меры, предъявляет непокрытую часть и переводит разговор к сокращению плана производства
mehanizm.why: меры закрывают меньшую часть объёма, а произведённый излишек утилизируется с прямыми затратами

drills.family_note: круг 103: каждая ось несёт напечатанный потолок и календарь — площадка садового центра «не больше +50%», реалистичный прирост «+15 п.п.», закупочный цикл сети год при закрытых листингах, посадка через шесть недель и два сезона роста; без применения этих условий сумма 431 тыс. против 1.8 млн не считается и разговор не переходит к сокращению плана посадки при 4 за утилизацию единицы

drills.title: Head Count
drills.prompt: Verandolk is the federal agency that runs the national parks. It is worried about retention among its Law Enforcement rangers and has just had a survey back from them. Brainstorm what the agency could do — and tell me which of your ideas you would take to the director first.
facts: The agency employs **2,100** Law Enforcement rangers. **98** of them left last year, and each departure costs the agency **$35,300**.
Law Enforcement rangers carry police- and firefighter-like duties and are trained in areas including wilderness medicine and search and rescue.
The survey put the rangers' pain points in three areas: family friendliness, effective senior leadership, and performance-based rewards.

Family friendliness: rangers are sometimes expected to move across the country to the middle of nowhere, where their children may have no access to schooling. Effective senior leadership: whether park superintendents have the background and experience to lead — most superintendents come up through the Education ranger track.

Performance-based rewards: the rangers are not primarily motivated by money, but they note that pay is higher at other government organisations and that those organisations also pay overtime, which this agency does not pay at all.

key.load:
**`LOAD` — the price of a retention idea is charged per ranger on the payroll; its saving is collected per ranger who would have left. The two bases are 2,100 and 98.**
The whole Law Enforcement bill is 98 × $35,300 = **$3,459,400 a year**. Spread over the 2,100 rangers who would have to receive any across-the-board benefit, that is **$1,647 per ranger per year** — and that is the ceiling for a measure that ends the leaving completely, which no measure does. The working conversion is smaller: one percentage point of attrition is 21 rangers, worth 21 × $35,300 = **$741,300 a year**, or **$353 per ranger per year** of budget. So the list splits not by which complaint an idea relieves but by **what an idea is charged per head of**: pay, overtime, insurance and tutoring are bought for all 2,100; assignment matching, local sourcing, a promotion track and mentoring are bought per posting, per seat or per person actually at risk, and face no such ceiling. Write the same measure service-wide and the ceiling falls to **$262 per head** — 23,608 rangers against a total bill of $6,175,400, because the 21,508 rangers added carry only $126 each. The measure has not changed; only the base it is charged to. The survey's three headings sort complaints, and complaints carry no price tags.
*Difference from the `MECH-76` slots (BR-009, BR-030): there the measure is aimed at the wrong segment because the economics differ by segment. Here the segment is right and the idea is right — what breaks it is that the payment is charged to the whole payroll while the saving is collected only from the few who would have gone.*
*Grounding: The National Park Service (W17) — the interviewer's note asks for the costs of the proposed solutions and a hypothesis of which is best; this slot turns that instruction into a number.*
key.cover:
**`COVER`:**

| Axis | What counts |
|---|---|
| **Size of the prize** | 98 × $35,300 = $3,459,400 a year; one point of attrition = 21 rangers = $741,300 = $353 per ranger-year |
| **What each idea is charged per head of** | the whole payroll of 2,100 (pay, overtime, benefits, tutoring) against per posting, per seat, per person at risk (matching, local sourcing, a promotion track, mentoring) |
| **What the survey already closed** | money is not the primary motivator; pay sits below other government organisations; overtime is paid at zero, not merely at a low level; superintendents come up through the Education track, so the ceiling is who fills the seat, not how the incumbent leads |
key.dead:
**`DEAD`:**

| Branch | What kills it |
|---|---|
| "Survey the rangers to find out why they leave" | the survey has been run and its three areas are a fact of the slot — fails `[GROUND]` |
| Contract law enforcement out to local police forces | answers a different question: the client asked how to keep its rangers, not how to stop employing them |
| Recruit harder / raise the intake to cover the losses | it buys the $35,300 instead of avoiding it; it keeps posts filled and leaves retention where it was |

**Echelon mechanic:** a balanced list — two or three ideas under each of the three named areas — reads as complete coverage and yields "take the strongest complaint first", and that conclusion is unpriced.

cull.new_fact: The finance office sends the same figures for the other three classifications: Education — 175 left of 3,750 rangers, at $6,200 per departure; Maintenance — 215 of 8,615, at $3,500; Administrative — 251 of 9,143, at $3,500.
team_ideas: Pay overtime to Law Enforcement rangers — the one reward item the survey records as not paid at all.
Take the case to the director on turnover rate: Law Enforcement is the classification bleeding fastest.
Give every ranger in the service the right to refuse one relocation without prejudice.
Start with the Administrative rangers: 251 of them left last year.
Fill Law Enforcement vacancies by transferring Maintenance and Administrative rangers across instead of recruiting outside.
Open a promotion track that takes Law Enforcement rangers to superintendent — a seat most of whose holders come up through the Education track.
cull.peridea_raw:
**Per-idea analysis — computed BEFORE the kill set is declared (`[CULL-PERIDEA]`):**

| # | Idea | What the fact does to it | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Overtime for Law Enforcement rangers | the fact does not touch it. The case prints no price for overtime anywhere, and an idea the record does not price is **priced, not culled** | alive |
| 2 | Take the case to the director on turnover rate | the table **denies the premise**: 175 of 3,750 Education rangers is 4.67%, the identical rate to 98 of 2,100. Law Enforcement is not the classification bleeding fastest; what distinguishes it is $35,300 against $6,200 | **killed** · `contradicts the fact` |
| 3 | Every ranger in the service may refuse one relocation | the fact does not touch it. Written service-wide and still alive: it carries no payment per head, so the size of the payroll does not price it | alive |
| 4 | Start with the Administrative rangers, 251 leavers | feasible, and the fact makes it look **better** — 251 is the largest count in the table. But the client asked about retention among Law Enforcement rangers, and this answers a different question | **killed** · `does not answer the question asked` |
| 5 | Transfer Maintenance and Administrative rangers into Law Enforcement posts | **the table does not settle it.** It cuts both ways on the figures given — the transfer removes an outside search for the Law Enforcement post and opens one in a column priced at $3,500 — and the fact contains nothing that decides which way. Its own measure of success, "fewer outside hires", comes out at zero on this table, and a benefit measured at zero is a reason to price and test the idea, not to strike it off | alive |
| 6 | A promotion track from Law Enforcement ranger to superintendent | the fact does not touch it | alive |

**Kill set: `{2, 4}` — derived from the table, not the other way round.**
**The grounds differ:** `2` — the table denies the idea's premise; `4` — the idea answers a different question from the one asked. Neither kill rests on an idea being expensive.

**Proof by contradiction, mandatory in a CULL slot:** if the rule were "anything naming another classification is dead", it would catch 4 — but 5 names Maintenance and Administrative and is alive. If the rule were "anything scoped to Law Enforcement survives", 2 would live. If the rule were "the superlatives are the kills", 1 ("the one reward item … not paid at all") and 6 ("most of whose holders") would die, and both are alive. Neither the scope word, nor the classification named, nor the grammar decides. What decides is whether the table leaves the idea's premise standing, and whether the idea is still aimed at the question that was asked.

**Expense is not a ground for culling.** The table makes every per-head measure dearer and kills none of them for it — the precedent is binding: BR-001 idea 6 ("economically weak, but weakness is not grounds for culling") and BR-004 idea 6 ("expensive and slow, but not killed by the fact"). The arithmetic of the base belongs to move 1 and to the recommendation, not to the kill set.

**Pass criteria, second move — the two rules apply to different things and never to the same thing.** The **set** is judged strictly: `{2, 4}` named exactly, one cut too many failing as hard as one missed. The **wording of a ground** is judged generously: a candidate who names a ground more precisely than this table records it is passed on that ground, not failed.

**`[NOSELF]`:** the table arrives as raw rows — counts, headcounts, unit costs. That the two rates are equal, and that the largest count and the largest bill sit in different columns, is assembled by the candidate.
